pages.text: These glyphs manipulate the capsum itself. More often than not, they do not modify species at all, just rearranging them on the stack. In many instances, these glyphs act on generic species, in these cases these species will be denoted with an uppercase letter of the Latin alphabet.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.swap
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)A, B$()$(br)Swaps the species at the head with the species below it.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.swap_ends
pages.text: $(n)D, …, A$() → $(n)A, …, D$()$(br)Swaps the ends of the capsum, with the head going to the end, and vice versa.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.dup
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)B, A, A$()$(br)Duplicates the species at the head of the capsum.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.drop
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)B$()$(br)Removes the head of the capsum and does not return anything at all.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.tuck
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)A, B, A$()$(br)Takes the species at the head of the capsum, and duplicates it, placing it below the species below the head in the pattern shown above.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.over
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)B, A, B$()$(br)Duplicates the species below the head onto the head, preserving the original two species.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.nip
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)A$()$(br)Pops the species below the head, returning nothing.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.fish
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)A$()$(br)Pops the species at the place, counting down from the head, corresponding to the number popped by the glyph$(br2)eg. 2 → species at the 2nd place, the one just below the head.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.peek_fish
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(n)A$()$(br)Similar to Fish, except the selected species is not popped, but just cloned, with the clone being placed onto the head instead.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.drop_at
pages.text: $(n)number$() → $(br)Pops the object at the place, counting down from the head corresponding to the number popped by the glyph.$(br2)eg. 2 → ; would pop the species at the 2nd place (just below the head), returning nothing.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.push_to
pages.text: $(n)A, number$() →$(br)Pops species A and places it in the place, counting from the head, corresponding to the number popped by the glyph.$(br2)Eg. $(n)C, B, A, 2$() → $(n)C, A, B$() (A is now at the 2nd place)

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.dup_to
pages.text: $(n)A, number$() →$(br)Pops species A and places it in the place, counting from the head, corresponding to the number popped by the glyph. It then restores A at the head, preventing consumption.$(br2)eg. $(n)C, B, A, 2$() → $(n)C, A, B, A$() (A is now at the 2nd place without counting the head)

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.swap2
pages.text: $(n)D, C, B, A$() → $(n)B, A, D C$()$(br)Swaps the top two pairs of species with each other. Preserves order within the pairs.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.dup2
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(n)B, A, B, A$()$(br)Duplicates the top two species, preserving the order within the pair.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.drop2
pages.text: $(n)B, A$() → $(br)Pops the top two species, returning nothing.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.clock_rot
pages.text: $(n)C, B, A$() → $(n)B, A, C$()$(br)Pops the third species and pushes it to the head, preserving the order of the head and the subsequent species. In short: the third species goes to the head.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.counter_rot
pages.text: $(n)C, B, A$() → $(n)A, C, B$()$(br)Pops the head and pushes it onto the third place, preserving the order of the (originally) second and third species. In short: the head goes to the third place.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.mass_dup
pages.text: $(n)A, number$() → $(n)A, A, …$()$(br)Duplicates the species below the head so its quantity matches the popped number$(br2)eg. $(n)A, 3$() → $(n)A, A, A$()

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.stack_size
pages.text: → $(n)number$()$(br)Pushes onto the capsum a number corresponding to the number of elements held within.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.print
pages.text: $(n)A$() →$(br)Prints the head of the capsum onto a text message viewable only by the caster.
